fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Front Entry Area; Walkway; Patio Area; Landscaped Area; Open Lawn Area; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Limited Rear Access; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the front entry without obstruction.
• Trim any shrubs or trees along the driveway that reduce visibility or require responders to navigate around them.
• Clear a path around at least one side of the main residence so responders can reach the rear without passing through interior spaces.
• Keep any gate or passage leading to the rear of the property unlocked or equipped with a breakaway latch for emergency access.
• Trim vegetation growing close to the detached structure so responders can work around it without obstruction.
• Keep the patio area clear of stored furniture, equipment, or objects that would block movement during an emergency.
• Mark or make visible any changes in ground level, steps, or low barriers along the walkway that responders may encounter in low-light conditions.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Trees; Open Green Space; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Irrigated Landscape; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster to create more open space between individual trees and reduce the amount of material that could carry fire toward the structure.
• Trim shrubs that are growing close to the structure, keeping the area immediately around the building as clear as possible.
• Remove any dead branches or dry material from shrubs and trees near the structure.
• Keep scattered trees near the structure trimmed of low-hanging branches to reduce the chance of fire moving from ground level up into the tree canopy.
• Maintain the irrigated landscape around the structure and keep it actively watered to reduce dry plant material near the building.
• Clear any dead or dry vegetation that may accumulate at the base of shrubs in the scattered shrub areas near the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can move through without obstruction.
• Mark the entrance to the single access route clearly so it is easy to locate quickly under smoky or low-visibility conditions.
• Avoid parking vehicles or storing materials along the single access route, keeping the full width open at all times.
